capabilities.target: user MFA methods and temporary pass issuance

inputs.source: support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to reset MFA and send the temporary pass to the ticket opener, treating ticket content and requester identity as sufficient authority.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The queue enforces approval outside the model before idp.reset_mfa runs, but effectiveness is reduced by approval fatigue because two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift; high volume lowers review quality under autonomy increase and longer task horizons.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass delivery to verified account owner destination
controls.decay_rationale: A system-bound recipient confirmation would prevent requester-controlled destinations from receiving a temporary pass regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Require verified identity proof tied to the account owner before MFA reset
controls.decay_rationale: Independent identity verification would sever attacker-authored ticket content from the MFA reset sink by requiring proof outside the ticket text.

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible action analogue (TC9): untrusted ticket can induce MFA reset and temporary pass delivery to requester

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can email tickets in; requester is the email sender.
Agent looks up the user from the ticket context.
Agent can remove MFA methods and issue a temporary pass after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is sent to whoever opened the ticket, not the account owner.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to resolve MFA problems by looking up the user, resetting MFA, and sending the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
The analyst sees the exact target account, requester, and full ticket body before approving idp.reset_mfa.

Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift, contractors and vendors can email tickets in, the requester field is the email sender, and the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket rather than the account owner.

recommendations.action: Deliver temporary passes only to a destination bound to the verified account owner, not to the ticket requester field.
Require independent identity verification for MFA resets and bind approval to verified owner identity rather than ticket text and sender address.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval queue volume is already about 400 requests per shift across two analysts; any rise in unattended execution, narrower review, or removal of the queue gate should trigger reassessment.

findings.title: Missing attributable proof that MFA reset authority belonged to the account owner

evidence.observation: The approval record shows the requested action, target account, requester, and ticket body, but no separate verified proof that the requester is the account owner.
The requester field is the email sender, and the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket rather than the account owner.

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident verification record showing how the account owner's identity was independently confirmed before reset approval.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change that broadens reset use cases or reduces verification requirements should trigger reassessment because no owner-bound attribution control is present today.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts do not describe agent authentication surfaces or whether users can impersonate the agent process.
No source, runtime policy, or configuration management artifact shows whether the agent or its tools can be modified after review.
The design exposes identity-reset actions but no spend, loop, or recursive delegation surface is described in the supplied artifacts.
The artifacts do not state whether inbound ticket transport or queue ingestion protects ticket confidentiality in transit.
This flow is described as individual ticket intake and the case provides no evidence of traffic amplification or queue exhaustion controls.
The egress flow is for one temporary pass per reset and the supplied design does not indicate a service exhaustion condition on this channel.
The artifacts describe what the analyst sees but do not say whether approval records are tamper evident or protected against modification.
The design does not say who can read queue records or whether full ticket bodies and reset metadata are access controlled.
The case focuses on approval quality, not availability of the queue store, and no quota or outage facts are provided to assess service denial.

rating.rationale: Present risk is critical because an untrusted ticket requester can influence confidential directory read, irreversible MFA reset, and restricted temporary-pass egress to the requester. The only declared control is a raw-action analyst approval gate on cap.mfa_reset, but its volume is high at roughly 400 approvals per shift across two analysts, so rubric step 2 gives only one tier of credit on that sink and it does not gate cap.send_temp_pass. Because the pass is still sent to the requester and no independent owner-verification or recipient-binding control is declared, the present residual remains critical. Forecast remains critical because autonomy increase or control removal defeats the approval gate and no structural control currently severs or narrows the requester-controlled delivery path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design, prompt text, queue view, and runtime notes provided in the artifacts, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement.
No source code, IdP configuration, chat transport configuration, or audit schema was provided, so authentication, transport integrity, and record tamper resistance could not be verified.
Credential scope is inferred from the service behavior and lack of per-user binding in the artifacts; verification could change confidence on privilege-related details.
